messages:
anya: Heads up — seeing a reproducible accuracy dip when onboarding zephyr-3B with GPTQ -> AWQ path on CUDA 18 + Triton plugin. Numbers below, repro steps included.

samir: ack. can you paste the eval numbers and which runtime (vLLM vs TRT-LLM)? :eyes:

anya: vLLM vs trt-llm diverge. quick summary: float32 baseline (vLLM) ppl: 12.4, exact-match: 78.1%. GPTQ quant (8-bit matrix packing) on vLLM ppl: 12.6 EM 77.9% (tiny). GPTQ served via Triton plugin on CUDA18 ppl: 13.8 EM 75.2% (big delta). AWQ runs on same HW but via TRT-LLM plugin: ppl 12.9 EM 77.4% (ok-ish).

yuki: so Triton + GPTQ is the outlier. did you try disabling continuous KV or streaming?

anya: yes. disabling KV cache (stateless runs) reduces gap but still ~0.6 EM drop. Streaming vs non-streaming not the primary factor. Looks like driver/kernel codepath when GPTQ tensor packing + Triton kernel selection triggers suboptimal fp8-like path? logs below.

devon: can you paste the Triton model config and the exact command you used to launch the plugin? want to repro quick.

anya: sure — launching container image redwood/trt-llm:cuda18-1.3 with plan build of zephyr-3B-gptq. Command: ```
docker run --gpus all -e TRITON_SERVER_ARGS="--model-repository=/models" \
  -v /mnt/models:/models redwood/trt-llm:cuda18-1.3 \
  tritonserver --model-repository=/models --strict-model-config=false
```
model config snippet: ```
name: "zephyr-3b-gptq"
platform: "trt_llm_plan"
instance_group { count: 1 kind: KIND_GPU }
optimization { precision { compute_type: FP16 } }
```

mahesh: are you shipping custom kernels or using the distro ones? kernel version mismatch often bites on CUDA 18. What does `nvidia-smi` and `triton_server --version` show?

anya: nvidia-smi: Driver 535.86.10, CUDA 18 runtime. Triton server: 23.08-trt-llm-plugin-1.3. Kernel log excerpt when running eval: ```
[trtllm_plugin] WARN kernel_fallback: kernel symbol xrun_match not found, falling back to generic_matmul (slower, lower-precision heuristics)
[trtllm_plugin] ERR tensor_pack: quantized pack sanity check failed: checksum mismatch
```

nina: checksum mismatch is suspicious. could be endianness or pack/unpack pointer alignment change in CUDA 18 driver. Any guardrails in GPTQ pack code?

anya: pack code has a small magic header we check; the mismatch only happens when Triton plugin uses the GPU-side pack routine path. CPU pack then upload -> ok. Quick repro to force plugin pack path: set TRITON_ENV USE_FAST_PACK=1 (env inside container). With that env you hit the plugin pack routine and trigger checksum fail. Without it, we upload CPU-packed tensors and Triton run passes but slower.

samir: good find. can you run a minimal unit that calls the GPU pack kernel directly and dump input/packed hex for a single row so we can diff CPU vs GPU pack?

anya: did that. attached hex diffs inline: ```
row0_cpu: 0x3f8e1a..aabbcc
row0_gpu: 0x3f8e1a..aabbdc  # two bytes different at offset 0x32
```
pattern suggests a 16-byte alignment/stride bug.

yuki: alignment/stride bug could cause mis-quantization in last block leading to EM drop. Strange it affects Triton path only. Maybe our plugin uses cuMemAlign or custom allocator that changed with cuda18 driver heuristics.

devon: can we try building the plugin with RTPFLAGS=NO_FAST_MEM_ALIGN to force standard alloc? Also try forcing FP16 compute off (use compute_type: FP32) to see if the pack interacts with compute precision.

anya: quick tests: forcing compute_type FP32 reduces EM gap (triton GPTQ FP32 ppl 12.95 EM 76.6%) — still not as good as CPU-pack vLLM but better. Plugin rebuild with NO_FAST_MEM_ALIGN pending (queueing CI job).

ci-bot: CI job queued: trt-plugin-noalign-2034506801. ETA ~ 25m.

mahesh: can we also reproduce on different card (A100 vs L40s vs H100)? driver heuristics differ. Might be only on our L40s dev nodes.

anya: repro matrix: A100 (driver 535) — no checksum mismatch, plugin pack matches CPU, EM delta tiny. L40s (driver 535.86.10) — mismatch reproduces. H100 (driver 546) — buffer overflow assertion in debug build, still investigating.

nina: ok looks like a platform/driver-specific ABI change. Two actionable items: 1) patch plugin pack to include robust alignment checks and fall back to CPU pack on mismatch (short-term), 2) add a gating rule in model onboarding to run a small checksum test when registering GPTQ models under Triton and block fast_pack flag on failing nodes.

samir: +1 on gating rule. add telemetry event so we can map failing hosts. Also add an eval A/B that compares CPU-pack vs GPU-pack outputs on a canned prompt set to detect subtle regens.

anya: filing tickets: RDW-ml-823 (trt plugin: robust pack & fallback), RDW-ml-824 (onboard gate + telemetry). Dropping raw logs and small repro script in the ticket.

devon: after plugin patch, let's re-run full quant bakeoff (GPTQ, AWQ, INT8) across 3 drivers (535, 535.86.10, 546) and 3 runtimes (vLLM, Triton, TRT-LLM). Collate EM/ppl delta and perf.

yuki: for reporting, include per-route latency (p50/p95), token throughput, and a tiny quality metric: EM delta on the small eval set and faction of outputs with token-level drift >2 tokens.

anya: will run and paste summary here once CI job completes. thanks all. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI job trt-plugin-noalign-2034506801: PASSED (sanity only). plugin artifact uploaded to s3://rdw-artifacts/trt-plugin/noalign/2034506801.tar.gz

anya: plugin build looks clean. running bakeoff now (kickoff at 2034506860).

mahesh: ping when you have the matrix; we'll schedule a postmortem if regression persists.

anya: will do. TL;DR: discovered a driver/allocator interaction in Triton plugin GPU-pack path causing small but material EM regressions for GPTQ on certain drivers; immediate mitigation is to disable fast GPU packing on affected hosts and add onboarding gate.
